title: Property checking and honest experiments
goal: Check the sorting contract independently of the timer and collect a reproducible measurement log.

prerequisites.text: Modules 1–3: validated input, functions, vector, records, references and lifetimes.
Direct learning dependencies: cpp.pseudo-random-numbers, cpp.recursion-divide-conquer. New constructs are explained before the task.

sections.title: Examples, properties and proofs
paragraphs: The row 3, 1, 3, −2 exercises duplicates and negatives. One example gives an observation, while a property defines a check for every valid row.

An example connects one input to an expected output. A property describes a class of inputs, such as sorted output preserving the input multiset. A proof explains why the algorithm satisfies the condition over its valid modeled domain. These forms of evidence complement one another; a passing test does not turn into a proof.

Start with independent small expectations: [3,1,3] must become [1,3,3], not [1,3]. Add general properties next. They can detect failures on unfamiliar data, but the properties themselves need scrutiny. For record sorting, keys alone are insufficient: check IDs and associated fields, using original labels to check stability.

sections.title: Oracles and independence
paragraphs: An oracle supplies an expected answer. It can be a linear scan for search, a hand-built table for small inputs, or a library sort plus multiset checks for an educational sort. Two copies of one function are not independent oracles. State the assumptions behind your chosen method.

Test properties against known-bad outputs too. An all-zero array may be ordered but lose the input; a reversed array can preserve multiplicities while violating order. Such negative controls show that the checker distinguishes substantive defects rather than always returning true.
Check ordering on neighboring pairs. Verify permutation separately, because an empty result also passes an order check.

sections.title: Metamorphic relations
paragraphs: When a large exact answer is inconvenient, relate several runs. Sorting an already sorted integer result should not change it: idempotence. A permutation or reversal of the input should sort to the same value array. Doubling each permitted integer preserves relative order provided arithmetic does not overflow.

A relation must fit the contract. Permuting input records can change the tied-label order of a stable sort, so entire-record output equality need not hold. Shifting all search keys requires shifting the target too. Justify the relation first, then test it under explicit arithmetic bounds.
Sorting an already sorted result leaves it unchanged. Reversing the original changes input order, but sorting gives the same result.

sections.title: Three properties across input classes
paragraphs: Inspect the checks on the row with two threes and predict the final counter.

reveal.title: Reveal the output and walkthrough
paragraphs: The program increments checked once per passing input. The line 5 properties reports five input sets, with properties checked inside each pass.

tables.caption: What happens at each step
rows: Neighbors are ordered and both threes survive.
The permuted input gives the same sorted row.

sections.title: Generation, shrinking and safe mutation
paragraphs: Combine fixed input classes with several saved seeds. Shrink a failing case by removing items or simplifying values while preserving failure, then keep the minimal case in regression. An extension exhaustively enumerates lengths up to six over {-1,0,1}: 1093 collections, not every input in the general domain.

A mutation is a small intentional implementation change that a test should detect. The example truncates a pass while keeping every index valid. Success means detecting the defect, not the mutant working correctly. Do not use an invalid std::sort comparator, out-of-bounds access or signed overflow as the mutation; a defined but wrong result is sufficient.
The mutant stops before the final pair. For [3, 1, 2] it leaves [1, 3, 2], and the check finds 3 > 2.

sections.title: A safe defect that must be detected
paragraphs: Trace the version with the wrong upper bound. Find the element that exposes the defect.

sections.title: Which clock and which region?
paragraphs: Use std::chrono::steady_clock for durations: its readings do not move backward as time progresses. end−start is a duration; duration_cast converts units. elapsed_ns names nanoseconds as a unit, not a promise of nanosecond resolution or accuracy. A very short measured interval may legitimately produce zero.

Copy input before start, then validate and write files after end. The measured region is the selected sort, not the whole process. C++ compilation, compiler download, UI and Worker startup are separate costs. End-to-end user latency needs another protocol, which this lab does not perform.
Use steady_clock for elapsed time. Make the copy before the first reading and check the result after the second.

sections.title: Warmup, repeats and uncontrolled factors
paragraphs: Before five recorded runs per algorithm, the lab performs one unrecorded warmup pass. Every run receives a fresh copy of base; otherwise insertion would see already sorted input after the first run. Validate every result so a fast wrong answer cannot enter the comparison table as an achievement.

The teaching code runs std_sort before insertion, which can itself introduce order bias. Browser load, scheduling, caches and compiler settings also affect observations. A serious comparison needs more sizes and input classes, run-order control, more repeats and environment details. Do not label this small protocol an already completed research benchmark.
Warm up each algorithm with a separate call. Each of its five recorded runs starts with the same original values.

sections.title: Raw samples and an honest conclusion
paragraphs: timings.tsv has ten rows after the header: algorithm, iteration, elapsed_ns. Check five distinct iterations 0…4 per algorithm and nonnegative integer durations. Native and WASI timing numbers are not required to match exactly. Retain all samples instead of only the most flattering minimum.

Median and spread help describe observations, but five values at one size give a limited picture. State size, data class, preparation and the exact timed region. Say so if differences are comparable to noise. O(n²) versus O(n log n) follows from models and growth reasoning; seconds can investigate a practical hypothesis without supplying that foundation.
When elapsed_ns is 0, the clock resolution may be insufficient for such a small input. Preserve the observation with the others.

sections.title: The final project and its defence
paragraphs: The project connects eight topics: catalogue validation, ID/value indexes, stable recursive merging, binary boundaries, frequencies and an RNG audit. Its report has deterministic ordering. A separate driver checks functions; the separate lab supplies raw timings. Do not link two mains or confuse saving an artifact with an automatic Cloud push.

In the defence, explain an index invariant, preparation/query costs, rejection without a partial report and a counterexample to a wrong solution. Then implement a small requirement with independent tests. Public cases and references support learning rather than a protected examination service; completed flags and passing runs do not automatically create mastery or a university grade.
The capstone combines experiment, correctness checks and limits. Begin with your own measurement log so the evidence is retained.

sections.title: Now try your own task
paragraphs: Separate property checks from timing. Save the ten observed durations and explain the limits of any conclusion.
Write the expected row for 4 3 1 3 -2 and a counterexample that drops a duplicate.

selfcheck.prompt: What does the program print when all five inputs pass their checks?
selfcheck.feedback: checked increments for each input that passes all checks, yielding 5 properties.

selfcheck.prompt: Is is_sorted sufficient for a correct sort?
options: No, element preservation is also needed
selfcheck.feedback: Deleting every element also gives a sorted result.
Sorting again leaves the resulting value order unchanged.

selfcheck.prompt: What is timed in the laboratory?
selfcheck.feedback: Copy preparation and checks are outside the clock boundaries.
Resolution and rounding can produce zero observed duration.
A small experiment cannot replace analysis and a representative benchmark.

selfcheck.prompt: Give a sorted output that should fail the permutation check for 3, 1, 3, −2.
selfcheck.feedback: For example −2, 1, 3. The order is correct, and one of the threes is missing.

practice.title: Laboratory: Property checking and honest experiments
practice.task: Read n=0…128 and n integers in −10000…10000 with no extra tokens. Compare std::sort and insertion on independent copies: one unrecorded warmup and five measurements each, with copying and validation outside timing. timings.tsv has header algorithm<TAB>iteration<TAB>elapsed_ns followed by five std_sort and five insertion rows, iteration=0…4 and nonnegative integer ns. Check ordering, preservation, idempotence and detection of a safe mutation. stdout: contracts PASS, samples 10, mutation detected on separate lines. Invalid input gives invalid.

walkthrough: data/records.txt: n=0…64 followed by n triples id word value; unique id in 1…9999, word uses a…z with length 1…12, value in −10000…10000. Whitespace separates tokens; lines do not define syntax and extra tokens are rejected.

stdin: at most 32 commands find id, range lo hi, freq word, audit seed or list. Require id=1…9999, −10000<=lo<=hi<=10000, seed=0…4294967295. Missing file gives open-failed; malformed data gives invalid-data; any invalid command gives invalid without a partial report.

index-report.txt contains records n, id rows ordered by id, value rows ordered by value with stable ties, sum and lexical word counts. Exact cases below define formatting. Run artifacts are not saved automatically: save them explicitly.

terms.definition: A statement about a class of inputs, such as multiset preservation.
An independent way to obtain the expected result.
A relation between results on transformed inputs when the full answer is unknown.
A controlled change to a correct program to evaluate tests.
A monotonic clock suitable for interval measurements.
An unrecorded preliminary run under an explicit policy.
Individual observations retained before computing summaries.
Matching the scope of a claim to the experiment actually performed.

visualization.title: Property checking and honest experiments
visualization.description: A textual step model of the concepts, not C++ execution or a performance measurement.

steps.description: An independent oracle gives [1,2,3]. Record value-preservation requirements before timing.

steps.title: Mutant
steps.description: Skipping the last insertion leaves [1,3,2]. Accesses stay valid: this is a logical defect without UB.

steps.title: Detection
steps.description: The ordering check detects 3>2. Experiment success means the test rejected the mutant.

steps.title: 2 × 5 samples
steps.description: For two correct sorts, prepare fresh copies outside timing, perform warmup and retain ten ns durations.

steps.title: Limited claim
steps.description: timings.tsv retains raw nonnegative numbers, including valid zero. Five small runs do not establish universal algorithm superiority.
